prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form that made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B041 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case. The discovery changed the field in a way that is easy to state: a gut hormone was shown to be a physiological incretin and satiety signal, its biologically active (7-36) form was identified, and that knowledge is what made a labile peptide into a drug class. The clinical consequence is large, confirmed by several independent drugs and by outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease, and the work is decades old, so maturity is not a concern. I considered a two-part prize with B030, as the chair asks. It would force B041 down to two names and would require choosing between Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, each of whom represents a distinct step the citation can name. I find no scientific reason to impose that cut on a discovery that is already complete in itself, and the three-person limit is better spent on one coherent achievement than on two thinner ones.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point, and the round-1 files sharpened it rather than resolving it. Four credited names compete for three places, and Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is what put the drugs in patients' hands. I cannot verify Mojsov's priority for the active peptide, nor the claims of Habener and others outside the credited list, from the material I am allowed to read, and I am not willing to claim a resolution I do not have. I also accept the point made by Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson that calling Knudsen's work merely industrial is unfair; excluding her is a judgment about which steps a citation can name as discoveries, and it carries a real cost. If the committee decides the achievement is the drug, my trio is the wrong trio, and I would then want that argued openly rather than by default. The second weakness is that a prize so close to commercial success could be read as honouring impact rather than discovery.

responses.point: Calling Knudsen's work translational understates it, since the drugs that changed care are her designs, and the exclusion should be admitted as a real gap rather than dismissed as industrial.
responses.response: I agree, and in round 1 I did not make this point as clearly as you did. I withdraw any suggestion that her work belongs on the lesser side of a line between science and industry. Medicinal chemistry that turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug is a scientific achievement. My position is narrower: a citation about the physiology and active form of GLP-1 names Holst, Mojsov and Drucker, and a citation about the drugs would name different people. I would not blur the two. If the committee chose the second, I would not assume Mojsov is the one to yield, as I said before; I would ask which of the three has the weakest documented link to the drug-making step, and I cannot answer that from these files.

responses.point: Knudsen's role, though industrial, is not obviously lesser than Mojsov's, so the choice should be argued on which steps a citation can name as discoveries; the chair also asks whether a single-achievement B041 is preferable to a two-part prize.
responses.response: I accept that framing and have changed how I defend the trio. My round-1 text leaned on the idea that physiology is the discovery and the drug is the product. The sharper argument is the one you give: ask which steps a citation can honestly call discoveries. Incretin physiology, the active peptide and the broader biology qualify. Long-acting design is also a discovery of a kind, but a different one, and it cannot be added without displacing someone. On your two-part question, I prefer the single part. Two parts would leave B041 with two names, and I see no documented ground in the record for removing Holst, Drucker or Mojsov. A second part must therefore justify itself on its own merits, and B030 would be the only candidate I would consider.

responses.point: CAR-T is equally mature with a clearer concept-to-clinic story for the credited names, so waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit dispute cannot be resolved; Sandberg also moved toward the June and Sadelain pairing.
responses.response: I share your view that B030 is the strongest alternative and that the two-name version is more defensible than the three-name list, so your move there is welcome. I disagree that the B041 credit dispute is a reason to wait. The dispute concerns which three of four people to name, not whether the discovery is complete, and delay does not give the committee evidence that it lacks now. CAR-T has its own gap, since the originators of the chimeric receptor concept, notably Eshhar, are outside the credited names, so the attribution risk there is not clearly smaller. I would also not make the choice depend on which prize is easier to write. Both stand ready, and B041 is stronger on originality and breadth.

responses.point: Rosenberg's adoptive transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials set the clinical proof of concept that made CAR-T credible and should not be dismissed.
responses.response: That is a fair correction to how I phrased round 1. I do not dismiss Rosenberg; his work on adoptive transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials is a real precondition for the field, and I treat it as part of the lineage. My concern is what a citation can say. The CAR design, costimulation and the first durable CD19 remissions belong to June and Sadelain, while the chimeric-receptor concept lies with Eshhar and colleagues outside the list. Adding Rosenberg makes a three-name citation for a lineage and not for a single discovery. If B030 came up, I would still prefer two names and an explicit acknowledgement of what is left out, but I accept that a reasonable member could place him inside.

responses.point: Imatinib (B023) is mature, but its reliance on prior chromosomal and kinase biology and on industrial chemistry makes a three-person split harder than for GLP-1; optogenetics is a credible second only with caution about field bias.
responses.response: Your point about B023 is correct, and it is why I keep it as the second alternative and not as a rival to B041. The line from the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL to Druker, Sawyers and Lydon is long and the prior discoverers are outside the list, so I would not claim a cleaner split there than for GLP-1. I still think it is very mature and its time is not later than that of B041. On optogenetics I appreciate that you named your field proximity yourself. I do not think it settles the question either way; the issue for me remains six credited names, a tool whose clinical effect is early, and no trio that avoids leaving out Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck.

uncertainties: Whether Knudsen should displace one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov if the committee anchors the citation in the drugs, and on what documented grounds, since I have none that identify the least central of the three.
Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and the roles of Habener and others outside the credited list, which I cannot verify from the files I am allowed to read.
Whether a second part (B030 limited to June and Sadelain) would be preferable to a single-part B041 if the committee found B041 could carry only two names.
Whether the strongest alternative should be chosen on clinical maturity (B030, B023) or on mechanistic clarity (B035), which I resolve toward clinical maturity but not with high confidence.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict specific to B041, B030, B023 or other shortlisted candidates is apparent from my profile. For transparency, my profile records past nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans (not a credited name on the shortlist), about twenty co-authored works with Per Svenningsson and one with Abdel El Manira (2009); none bears on a shortlisted candidate. My formal voting status as Secretary is not stated in my profile; I take the chair's note that all six members vote. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
